title: Flow guard rail and soft-quota orchestrator for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a Flow Guard Rail subsystem for Dedicated fleets that provides soft per-tenant throughput reservations, progressive overload shedding, and coordinated interaction with the predictive autoscaler. The subsystem should enable predictable minimum throughput for paying customers while allowing graceful degradation and capacity reclamation during cross-tenant contention.
background: Customers running Dedicated pools have requested stronger predictability guarantees for baseline throughput while preserving overall fleet efficiency. Existing admission controllers provide per-request rate limiting and simple queueing, but we lack a single orchestrator that combines soft reservations, staged backpressure, and autoscaler-informed headroom to meet SLOs without excessive over-provisioning.
goals: Provide soft guaranteed throughput per tenant (configurable token rate + burst budget)
Implement a staged queue with priority decay to avoid starvation of low-volume tenants
Integrate with predictive autoscaler to reserve headroom and preemptively relax shedding
Expose metrics and console dashboards for token-utilization, shed-rate, and headroom forecast
Support policy-driven fallbacks: model-variant downgrade, synchronous->async conversion, and reroute to fallback pools
non_goals: Replace hard SLA-backed reservation contracts (this is a soft-guarantee layer)
Implement end-to-end billing integration (will surface usage events for downstream billing work)
Large refactor of existing autoscaler logic (we will integrate via a defined API)
success_metrics: P99 tail latency for P0 tenants remains within 1.5x baseline under up to 60% cross-tenant load spikes
Shed-rate reduction for critical tenants vs today: target <= 0.5% during peak
Reduction in emergency manual capacity increases by 40% over next quarter
Dashboard adoption: >75% of Dedicated customers with soft guarantees enabled view headroom forecasts within first month
architecture_summary: Flow Guard Rail sits as an admission layer in front of the serving runtime for Dedicated pools. It maintains per-tenant token buckets (soft tokens + burst credits) and a staged in-memory queue. A scheduling loop consults autoscaler headroom signals and a predictive model to adjust per-tenant throttles and to decide eviction/shred policies. When shedding is required, a multi-stage strategy is used: 1) gentle slow-down via token refill throttling, 2) convert best-effort requests to async queue with retry tokens, 3) model-variant downgrade, 4) last-resort drop with reason codes. All decisions emit structured events for tracing and billing.
acceptance_criteria: Unit+integration tests for token accounting and priority decay logic
Load test demonstrating soft-guarantee preservation for configured tenants under synthetic spike
Autoscaler integration tests: headroom signals cause immediate refill-percentage adjustments
Console surface: per-tenant token utilization and a headroom forecast widget
Operational runbook documenting failure modes and rollback steps
implementation_notes: Use existing admission API layer as extension point; avoid touching serving runtime internals
Implement token store in memory with optional Redis backing for cross-node state (feature flagged)
Predictive autoscaler interface: HTTP endpoint returning reserved_headroom_pct and time_horizon_seconds
Keep control loop at 100ms cadence for responsive shedding; batch evaluations to reduce CPU overhead
Telemetry: emit token_acquire, token_release, shed_decision, fallback_action events with tenant_id and reason
Start with per-fleet non-global defaults; expose tenant config via Dedicated Console and API
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal canary on staging fleet with synthetic tenants (2 weeks)
Beta: opt-in for 5 paying customers (progressively broaden over 6 weeks)
Observability gating: if shed-rate for opted tenants >1% for 48h, pause expansion
Full rollout: enable by default for new Dedicated pools after 10-week stabilization window
Emergency disable: control-plane feature flag to bypass Flow Guard Rail instantly
testing_plan: Unit tests for accounting math, priority decay, and fallback selection
Chaos tests: simulate network partitions between autoscaler and guard-rail, validate safe defaults
Load tests: mixed-tenancy traffic with varying QPS distributions and request cost profiles
E2E: tenant-level SLO verification under synthetic model-heavy workloads
Security review: ensure event emission does not include sensitive prompt content
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: shed-rate > 0.5% for >5 minutes for any P0 tenant
Health check: control loop iterations > 95% success rate; otherwise page on-call
Telemetry retention: 30d for token-level events, 90d aggregated metrics
